Crawford County Tax Sales: How to Find Property Deals Few People Know About

Introduction

If you’re looking to invest in tax deed properties in Georgia, Crawford County might be one of the best places to start. Tucked between Macon and Columbus, this quiet county offers less competition, affordable properties, and a simple auction process—perfect for both new and experienced investors.

Brief Overview of Georgia’s Tax Deed Investing

In Georgia, tax sales follow a non-judicial tax deed process. That means when someone doesn’t pay their property taxes, the county auctions off the property—not just a lien. The original owner has one year and one day to pay you back, with a flat 20% penalty. If they don’t redeem, you can start the foreclosure process.

Important Details About Crawford County, GA Tax Sales

Why Georgia is a Good State for Tax Sale Investing

Georgia’s tax deed process is simple. You’re buying the actual property, not a certificate. With a flat 20% penalty and a shorter redemption period, investors can see fast, strong returns if the property is redeemed—and a clear path to ownership if not.

Fun Facts About Georgia

  • Georgia has a population of over 11 million people.
  • It has one of the shortest redemption periods among U.S. states: just one year and one day.
  • Georgia allows counties to hold non-judicial tax sales, which are faster than court-ordered sales.
  • Many investors overlook smaller counties like Crawford, even though they offer lower prices and less competition.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

Popular Attractions

Georgia offers:

  • Parks and hiking trails
  • Historic sites and museums
  • Theaters and seasonal festivals

Transportation

  • Interstate access via I-75 and I-16
  • Rail freight lines run through central Georgia
  • Regional airports in Macon and nearby cities

Economic Development

  • Agriculture is a leading industry in Crawford County
  • Growth in logistics and light manufacturing
  • Macon nearby offers more employment and housing demand

Community Appeal

  • Outdoor activities like hunting, fishing, and boating
  • Small-town living with friendly communities
  • Lower cost of living than metro areas

Why Crawford County Is Ideal for Tax Deed Investors

Crawford County is a good place for investors who want to avoid large crowds and high starting bids. It’s close enough to cities for resale or rental opportunities, but far enough to stay quiet and affordable.

What Makes Crawford County Tax Deeds a Smart Investment

High Returns with Lower Risk

When a property is redeemed, you earn a 20% penalty—no matter how quickly the owner redeems. If not redeemed, you may gain ownership after the redemption period.

Auction Process

  • Auctions are held outside the courthouse on the first Tuesday of the month.
  • Bidding starts at the amount of back taxes and fees.
  • Highest bidder wins and must pay in full immediately.

Maximum Returns

You can earn a full 20% return if the property is redeemed. If not, the foreclosure path begins, and you may end up owning the property free and clear.

Open to All Investors

Crawford County welcomes both local and out-of-state investors. You don’t need to live in Georgia to participate.

Understanding the Tax Sale Process in Crawford County

  1. Property owner fails to pay taxes.
  2. County posts a legal notice in The Georgia Post.
  3. Auction is held on the courthouse steps.
  4. You register 30 minutes before it starts.
  5. Pay with certified funds if you win.
  6. Wait one year and one day for redemption.
  7. If not redeemed, begin foreclosure to take full ownership.

Importance of Due Diligence

What to Do Before You Bid

  • Use QPublic Property Search to check the parcel.
  • Drive by the property, but don’t enter.
  • Look for possible liens or building issues.
  • Ask the Tax Office for updates before the auction.

What Happens If You Skip It

You could end up with:

  • A landlocked lot
  • A house that needs to be torn down
  • Utility or code enforcement liens you didn’t know about

Buying Over-the-Counter (OTC) Properties

How It Works

If a property doesn’t sell at auction, the county may offer it over-the-counter. Contact the Tax Commissioner’s Office to see if any OTC properties are available.

Benefits

  • No bidding competition
  • Fixed prices
  • Good options for long-term investors

Why Georgia Is a Top Choice for Tax Sale Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • Lower property taxes compared to many states
  • Easy rules for new investors
  • No transfer tax at tax deed sales

Real Estate Market Overview

  • Strong demand in nearby Macon
  • Crawford County offers affordable land and homes
  • Rental and resale opportunities nearby

Conclusion

Crawford County gives investors a chance to enter the Georgia tax sale market with lower risks and simple rules. With smaller crowds, lower prices, and the potential for solid returns, it’s worth your time—especially if you’re new to investing.

But don’t skip your research. Good due diligence leads to good deals.

Pro Tips

  • Double-check sale listings the day before. Counties can make last-minute changes.
  • Visit properties from the street to assess condition and location.
  • Get familiar with foreclosure steps in Georgia before buying.
  • Plan for repairs or holding costs if you end up with the property.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to live in Georgia to invest?
No. Anyone can participate in the auction, including out-of-state and international investors.

Can I walk onto the property before bidding?
No. You can only view from the street.

What happens if the property is redeemed?
You get your bid amount back plus a 20% penalty.

What if the property doesn’t get redeemed?
You can start the foreclosure process after one year and one day.

Are there other costs besides the bid?
Yes. You may need to pay for quiet title action, maintenance, or unpaid bills.
